title: Microburst elastic-horizon coalescer with soft-KV pinning for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement an elastic horizon coalescer in the continuous batching scheduler that absorbs microbursts of short/long mixed requests by dynamically stretching slot horizons, combined with a soft-KV pinning mechanism that opportunistically reserves small KV regions for predicted long-context responses. Goal is to reduce tail latency regressions and decrease costly KV evictions during skewed dialogue workloads without sacrificing steady-state throughput.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for mixed prompt/response synthetic workload ≤ baseline + 5ms
P99 latency reduction of ≥ 10% for 90th-percentile microburst traffic (measured on canary cluster)
KV eviction events during 60s microburst tests reduced by ≥ 40% compared to current scheduler
GPU memory fragmentation metric (per-GPU free-slab variance) reduced by ≥ 20% under mixed-length traces
E2E throughput under steady traffic stays within ±3% of baseline
Feature toggle present for canary rollout and full rollback within 15 minutes
updates: 2026-02-15: Initial kickoff and design brainstorm with runtime, infra, and ML infra leads. Agreed on two primary levers: horizon elasticity and soft-KV pin reservations.
2026-02-20: Prototype sketch completed — horizon extension by up to 2x for idle slots plus microburst detection using sliding window of arrival rates (proto in branch rn/microburst-coalescer-draft)
2026-02-24: Microbench harness added (tools/perf/microburst-replay). First replay shows 12% drop in P99 but 6% throughput regression — investigating packing heuristics.

2026-02-27: Added soft-KV pinning prototype that marks small KV chunks as 'probationary-reserved' for 10–30s when a long-response candidate is predicted by length-classifier. Internal perf run reduced KV evictions by ~38% on bench trace.
2026-03-01: Design review with PM and Design. Approved canary plan and observability dashboard changes. Assigned Marco for implementation of allocator changes and Riley for telemetry dashboards.
2026-03-01: Blocking item discovered — current slab allocator API does not expose per-slab residency metrics; opened ENG-561240 to add metric hooks.
decisions: Use soft-KV pinning (probationary, time-limited reservation) rather than hard reservation to avoid underutilized memory in low-load periods.
Horizon elasticity will be additive (extend horizon length) and bounded (max 2x nominal slot length) to cap latency amplification for short requests.
Microburst detection uses exponential-weighted arrival rate estimator (alpha=0.3) over 2s windows to trigger coalescing logic, tuned to minimize false positives.
Keep default behavior unchanged behind feature flag; enable on dedicated canary pool first.
tradeoffs: Elastic horizons can increase queueing latency for short prompts under some conditions — we cap elasticity and track short-request impact in tests.
Soft-KV pinning may cause slight memory underutilization during prolonged low activity but avoids heavy eviction churn during spikes.
Adding KV pinning complexity increases edge cases for eviction policies; we mitigate with probationary timers and strict telemetry to detect overdue pins.
Instrumentation and extra metrics add cost to runtime path; we attempt to batch metric emissions and rely on counters sampled at 100ms granularity.
testing_plan: Unit tests: horizon extension math, microburst detector thresholds, and probationary KV state transitions.
Integration tests: scheduler + allocator + runtime with synthetic traces (mixed short/long sequences, dialogue bursts, cold-starts).
Perf tests: replay production traffic (two week anonymized sample) and synthetic microburst scenarios at 10x normal arrival rates.
Canary rollout: enable feature flag for 2 beefy Dedicated machines (canary-tier-2) for 72 hours with detailed telemetry retention.
A/B experiment: 5% of traffic on a dedicated region routed to new scheduler, monitor P50/P95/P99, KV-evictions, GPU-fragmentation, and cost per token for 1 week.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge feature-gated implementation behind runtime flag. Internal QA for unit/integration tests.
Phase 1: Enable on internal perf harness and run 24-hour stress tests across representative clusters.
Phase 2: Canary enable on canary-tier-2 (2 hosts) for 72 hours. Collect dashboards and unblockers.
Phase 3: A/B 5% production traffic in non-critical region for 7 days. Evaluate metrics and customer impact.
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% in region, then global roll with staggered regions, monitor for rollbacks.
Rollback plan: disable flag and evict probationary pins, triggering immediate KV eviction normalization.
